findings.evidence: Line 107-119: `loginWithGoogle()` throws `new Error("Google sign-in not configured. Install 'expo-auth-session' and '@react-native-google-signin/google-signin' packages.")`
findings.notes: Finding is still applicable; Google and Facebook social login are placeholder stubs that throw runtime errors. TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md §16 lists Expo SDK 57 and React Native 0.86.3 but does not mention specific social auth packages; target is reasonable for an e-commerce mobile app.

findings.evidence: Line 121: `const { TapSDK } = require("@tap-as/sdk-react-native");` — dynamic require without package being listed in package.json. Same pattern repeats at line 163 for PayTabs and line 204 for Thawani.
findings.notes: All three regional payment SDKs are dynamically required but absent from package.json; they will crash with 'module not found' if invoked. TECHNOLOGY_STACK.md §6 lists Tap/PayTabs/Thawani as direct REST via httpx for backend; mobile SDK wrappers are not in the canonical stack.

findings.evidence: Line 139-145: `socialSignIn` throws `new SocialSignInError(`${SOCIAL_PROVIDER_LABELS[provider]} sign-in isn't available in this environment yet.`, provider, false)` for any non-google provider on native/web.
findings.notes: Facebook and Apple sign-in are non-functional stubs on all platforms; only Google GSI works on web. Target aligns with common mobile social auth patterns but is not explicitly mandated by benchmark docs.
